topics.topic: Allowed api_base_url forms, canonicalization, and operation-path joining
questions: Are userinfo, query, fragment, an existing base path, non-ASCII hosts, percent escapes and multiple trailing slashes allowed in `api_base_url`, and exactly how are they serialized and joined?
Are user information, query strings, fragments, percent-encoded separators and a base path allowed in `api_base_url`, and exactly how are they combined with the operation path?
Which URL components and canonical forms are allowed in api_base_url, and what exact joining rule applies?

judgement.why: The URL-form and joining passage was unchanged by the reopening change.

topics.topic: Encoding and truncation of arbitrary HTTP error bodies into failure_detail
questions: How is an arbitrary non-UTF-8 error body represented as textual `failure_detail`?
How is an arbitrary binary or invalid-UTF-8 error body represented in `failure_detail`?
How are arbitrary response bytes decoded and truncated into failure_detail?

quotes:
The body of
   an error response is not interpreted; at most `failure_detail_bytes_max` of it
   is kept as `failure_detail`, whose class is the highest of the execution's
   class and the classes the binding declares for its outputs, under A07 rule 5.
judgement.why: The error-body representation passage was unchanged by the reopening change.

topics.topic: Enforceable determinism boundary for clocks, randomness, concurrency, and other nondeterministic facilities
questions: What happens to CPython clock or entropy APIs omitted from the closed list, such as `time.clock_gettime`, `time.thread_time`, `os.times` or `ssl.RAND_bytes`?

Are implementations allowed to use concurrency or other scheduler-dependent standard-library behavior that can produce different results for the same input, and if so how can admission remain deterministic?
Are all ways of observing time forbidden, or only the entry points explicitly listed in A03?
What exact determinism guarantee must the sandbox enforce, and how are permitted nondeterministic Python or OS observations handled?
What complete enforceable boundary makes execution deterministic, and what is the required outcome when code uses an unlisted nondeterministic facility?

quotes:
The list is closed for the release; an
   entry point found missing is added by a new release.
judgement.why: The stated determinism boundary and closed trap list were unchanged by the reopening change.

topics.topic: Filesystem access permitted to sandboxed function code
questions: May implementation code itself read and write arbitrary files in the exchange directory or read runtime files, or must filesystem access be confined to the runner that transfers declared inputs and outputs?
May implementation code create, read, enumerate or modify files in the exchange directory, or is that directory accessible only to the runner?
May function code read runtime files or create/read arbitrary files in the exchange directory, or must filesystem access be limited to the files representing its declared inputs and outputs?

quotes:
No host directory is mounted except the read-only
   runtime and that exchange directory.
judgement.why: The sandbox filesystem-access passage was unchanged by the reopening change.

topics.topic: Immutable manifest file lookup by repository location and revision
questions: How does the kernel read a file at a repository revision without changing the working tree, and what kinds of location and revision are valid?
How does the kernel resolve a file at a revision, and what is refused when the location is not a repository, the revision is missing, or the working tree differs?
What exact mechanism maps manifest_location plus manifest_revision to immutable file bytes?

quotes:
`manifest_location`, `manifest_revision`: where the platform manifest is read
  and the repository revision it is read at — read by every manifest reading
  (M10), so a record changes for the kernel only when the owner changes the
  configured revision;
judgement.why: The manifest location-and-revision passage was unchanged by the reopening change.

topics.topic: Allowed carriage and cardinality for path-placeholder input ports
questions: Must a path-placeholder input also have `value` carriage, or may a file port with a string/integer schema be accepted at proposal time only to fail every send?
Must every input used by a path placeholder have cardinality one at binding proposal time?

judgement.why: The placeholder-port requirements were unchanged by the reopening change.

topics.topic: Approval identity and behavior when the rebuilt request differs
questions: When the owner approves a requested approval but the rebuilt request has changed, does the approval action send, fail, or merely create a new approval request?
Does a changed multipart boundary or resulting Content-Length make a request different for approval purposes?

quotes:
the kernel proceeds as if it did not exist — under a grant
   when one applies, otherwise by asking anew as rule 2 says;

The body is described as the JSON body's bytes, or for
   `multipart/form-data` as the parts in order, each as its name, filename when
   present, media type and the SHA-256 of its content, so the boundary is not
   part of it: equal parts give equal descriptions.
judgement.why: Both request-mismatch handling and multipart approval identity were unchanged by the reopening change.

topics.topic: Declared media-type syntax, canonicalization, parameters, limits, and equality
questions: What syntax and length must a declared media type satisfy before it is copied into an HTTP header, and are parameters permitted?
What media types may be declared, how are they canonicalized, and what equality rule is used by proofs and HTTP validation?

quotes:
a `file` port declares exactly one media type and a `value`
   port none;
judgement.why: The media-type declaration passage was unchanged by the reopening change.

topics.topic: How plain-HTTP loopback eligibility is determined
questions: Is loopback determined from a literal IP address in the URL, from DNS resolution, or from the actual connected address, and how are IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses handled?
Does this mean only a literal loopback IP, or also names such as `localhost` or any hostname that resolves to loopback, and when is resolution checked?

quotes:
Plain `http` is allowed only for an instance of
   class `local_dev` or `disposable_rig`, as the manifest instance's `class`
   states — an absent or unknown class counts as `production` — or one whose
   `api_base_url` host is a loopback address; any other plain `http` target is refused before sending.
judgement.why: The loopback-eligibility passage was unchanged by the reopening change.

topics.topic: Injection-safe multipart field-name encoding and boundary construction
questions: How are quotes, backslashes, controls and non-ASCII characters in port names escaped, how is the boundary chosen, and how are boundary collisions with file or value content prevented?
What port-name grammar or escaping algorithm makes multipart headers unambiguous and injection-safe?

quotes:
Each part has exactly two
   headers: `Content-Disposition: form-data; name="<port>"`, with
   `filename="<port>"` added for a file part, and `Content-Type`, the port's
   media type for a file part and `application/json` for a value part, without
   parameters; nothing else.
judgement.why: The multipart construction passage was unchanged by the reopening change.

topics.topic: Measurement and observable classification of sandbox resource-limit violations
questions: Are memory and process limits per process or aggregate across the whole sandbox, what counts toward scratch usage, and what observable event proves each limit was hit?
What observable evidence constitutes each limit being hit, including when user code catches the error, and how is it distinguished from crashed?

quotes:
ResourceBounds M04 are enforced from outside the environment with `setrlimit`
   (address space, processes) and the parent's own wall deadline and output
   count.
judgement.why: The resource-limit enforcement passage was unchanged by the reopening change.

topics.topic: Ownership and permission requirements for private data-directory artifacts
questions: Which ownership and permission modes satisfy “private,” including group permissions, ACLs, hard links and files owned by another user?
Which owners and permission bits count as private for directories, database files, lock files, value files and spool files?

quotes:
The directory and everything in it
   are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.
judgement.why: The data-directory privacy requirement was unchanged by the reopening change.

topics.topic: Pinned release dependency closure including bubblewrap and runtime versions
questions: Is the bubblewrap version also pinned or constrained, and what happens when the host supplies another version?
What exact runtime, bubblewrap and kernel dependency versions constitute release v1?

quotes:
A release pins the exact versions of the kernel's Python dependencies and of
   the sandbox runtime (A03); the sandbox interpreter of release v1 is CPython
   3.12, whose `random` module gives A03 rule 4 its list.
judgement.why: The release dependency-pinning passage was unchanged by the reopening change.

topics.topic: Preventing service credentials from leaking through responses, diagnostics, exceptions, or logs
questions: What must the kernel do if a service echoes the credential value in an error or successful response?
How must credentials be prevented from entering error excerpts, exceptions and logs?

quotes:
It never enters the store, a record, a trace, a preview, a
   failure detail, a log line, a process argument or a response.
judgement.why: The credential non-disclosure guarantee was unchanged, and the new credential-resolution checks did not make response echoing newly material.

topics.topic: Representation and validity of empty flow node identifiers versus endpoints
questions: May a flow node use the empty string, and if so how is it distinguished and ordered against flow endpoints?
Are empty node identifiers forbidden, or are flow endpoints represented by a separate tagged form?

quotes:
A flow input
   or flow output endpoint has the empty string as its node, so it orders before
   every node.
judgement.why: The empty-string endpoint representation was unchanged by the reopening change.

topics.topic: Required key sets for authored trial inputs and expected outputs
questions: Must authored inputs contain every input port exactly once, and must present `expected_outputs` contain every output port exactly once, or are partial and extra maps allowed?
What exact key set is required for trial inputs and for a present expected_outputs object?

quotes:
Either
   way it is added only when its input values fit the contract version's input
   ports, its expected outputs, when present, fit the output ports, and every
   value is within `stored_value_bytes_max` and every file within
   `trial_fixture_bytes_max` — the first failing condition in this order is
   named, ports taken in name order and, for one port, presence, carriage,
   schema, then size.
judgement.why: The authored trial-value validation passage was unchanged by the reopening change.

topics.topic: Validity of existing admissions after runtime or sandbox dependency upgrades
questions: After a kernel upgrade changes Python or other sandbox dependencies, may an old implementation continue using its old AdmissionVerdict even though real executions now use a different runtime?
After upgrading the Python runtime or sandbox dependencies, do existing admitted implementations remain active, require re-admission, or execute under their original runtime?

quotes:
A release pins the exact versions of the kernel's Python dependencies and of
   the sandbox runtime (A03); the sandbox interpreter of release v1 is CPython
   3.12, whose `random` module gives A03 rule 4 its list.
judgement.why: The release/runtime relationship was unchanged by the reopening change.

topics.topic: Whether every configured service must have credentials at startup
questions: Is a credential mandatory for every configured service at kernel startup, or may it be absent until an invocation fails?
May a configured service omit a credential, and if so is omission accepted at startup or refused only when an invocation is built?

quotes:
The installation's configuration file holds the owner token, the agent tokens
   and, per service, the selected manifest instance name and one credential: a
   header name — an HTTP field-name token, or the kernel refuses to start —
   and the reference that resolves to its value on the host;

a
   service the installation gives no credential, or whose secret file is
   missing, unreadable or holds an empty value or a control character, fails
   that request's pre-send check `credential_unresolved` and stops nothing
   else
judgement.why: Rule 1 requires one credential per configured service at startup, while the changed rule 2 permits a service to have no credential and defers refusal until request construction.

topics.topic: Application of value_schema to many-cardinality ports
questions: For a `many` value port, is `value_schema` applied to each element or to the array as a whole, especially when the schema itself has type `array`?

topics.topic: Canonical ordering and tie-breaking for flow validation failures
questions: How are two distinct edges with the same four endpoint fields, or two distinct constants with the same target, ordered for hashing and for selecting the first failure?
If the same smallest name is repeated in both the input and output directions, which failure is reported first?

topics.topic: Classification and accounting of outputs that cannot be represented as canonical JSON
questions: How is an output counted and classified when it is not representable as canonical JSON, such as a set, custom object, non-finite float or cyclic structure?

topics.topic: Classification of interrupted response bodies after final HTTP status and headers
questions: How is a timeout, reset or premature EOF while reading the body classified after a valid final 2xx status and headers have already arrived?

topics.topic: Complete manifest schema, validation order, and malformed-field classification
questions: What complete manifest schema is validated, in what order, and how are malformed-but-valid-JSON field types classified?

topics.topic: Credential-reference forms and secure resolution of secret files
questions: What forms of credential reference are valid, how are they resolved, and what ownership, permission and symlink checks apply to the referenced secret file?

topics.topic: Decoding credential-file bytes into an HTTP header value
questions: How are credential-file bytes converted to an HTTP header value?

topics.topic: Definition of arrival order for concurrent MCP requests
questions: For concurrently received MCP requests, what event establishes arrival order: first byte, complete frame, successful parse, authentication completion or insertion into an internal queue?

topics.topic: Derivation of an element's current conclusion from attempts and resolutions
questions: How is the current conclusion derived from an element’s ordered sequence of attempts and resolutions?

topics.topic: Eligibility to capture failed executions after a run is refused or cancelled
questions: May a value-only failed function execution be captured after its run ended `refused` or `cancelled`, or is every such capture refused because the run no longer holds a spool?

topics.topic: Equality semantics for guarded-edge runtime values
questions: What equality rule determines whether a runtime JSON value equals a guard value, especially for numbers such as `1` and `1.0` and structured values?

topics.topic: Exact byte accounting and pre-parse enforcement of MCP request-size limits
questions: Does `surface_request_bytes_max` count the complete MCP/JSON-RPC frame, only operation parameters, transport framing, and any base64 expansion, and how is the size known before parsing?

topics.topic: Handling and validation order for response Content-Encoding
questions: What happens if a service nevertheless returns `Content-Encoding`, and is the body decoded before size, digest, JSON or file validation?

topics.topic: Handling oversized aggregate arrays from mapped value outputs
questions: What happens when individually valid mapped results form an aggregate array larger than stored_value_bytes_max, and which NodeExecution records that failure?

topics.topic: Limits and failure outcome for untrusted HTTP status lines and headers
questions: What limit applies to the status line and response headers from an untrusted service, and what outcome results when that limit is exceeded?

topics.topic: Meaning of an earlier implementation for rollback eligibility
questions: What makes an implementation “earlier”: submission before the current implementation, a prior activation of that contract version, or merely any existing non-current implementation with a current-corpus admitted verdict?

topics.topic: Persistence and disclosure rules for TrialExecution failure details
questions: Do trial executions persist a failure detail, and if so what field and disclosure rules apply?

topics.topic: Privacy-preserving representation of approval request previews
questions: What redacted representation of a built request is returned to an agent so that personal data cannot leak indirectly through its URL, query, body or multipart description?

topics.topic: Recovery of the exact FlowActivation for draft writes
questions: How is the exact FlowActivation recovered after the same version has been activated multiple times or after a restart?

topics.topic: Retry and fresh-approval semantics after a direct not_applied outcome
questions: Can a direct 4xx `not_applied` attempt be resent in the same run, and if so which action requests that resend? Is a later equal run considered a resend requiring fresh approval?

topics.topic: Run termination when failed branches coexist with waiting branches
questions: If one independent branch has failed and another branch is waiting for approval or service recovery, does the run end `failed` immediately or remain waiting so that the independent branch can finish?

topics.topic: Scope and authentication requirements of list continuation tokens
questions: Can a continuation token from one list or query be reused for another, and what request facts must the token authenticate?

topics.topic: Scope and starting point of the HTTP transport timeout
questions: Does the timeout cover DNS resolution, connection, TLS, request upload and the complete response body as one deadline, and when exactly does that deadline begin?

topics.topic: Serialization and escaping of static paths and integer placeholder values
questions: What exact textual form is used for integer placeholder values, and what happens when the declared static path contains non-ASCII characters, spaces or existing percent escapes?

topics.topic: Size and count limits for manifest-derived URL and header metadata
questions: What size and count limits apply to manifest-derived URL and header material before a binding is proposed, accepted or sent?

topics.topic: Start and end points of the sandbox wall-time deadline
questions: Exactly when does `wall_time_ms` start and stop: before sandbox creation, before module loading, on entry to `run`, on its return, or only after cleanup finishes?

topics.topic: State retention and retry behavior after token-list reload failure
questions: What state and hash are retained after a failed configuration reread, and exactly when is the file retried?

topics.topic: Timestamp semantics for EffectAttempt owner resolution and conclusion
questions: Which timestamp records the owner's resolution, and does `concluded_at` mean the original unknown outcome time or the later resolution time?

topics.topic: Treatment of token-like or host-path-like strings in user-controlled data
questions: Does rule 7 also prohibit returning user-supplied text or values that happen to contain a token or host-path string, and if so how are they detected and represented?

topics.topic: Validation and actor resolution for hot-reloaded agent-token configuration
questions: May a hot-reloaded token list contain duplicate or missing agent names, invalid `may_author` values, or a missing owner token, and how is the actor determined then?

topics.topic: Whether and when an actively executing run may be cancelled
questions: Can the owner interrupt a run currently executing a function or HTTP request, or can cancellation apply only after the run has returned in a waiting state?
